More notably, unsupervised property-clustering performance improves by up to 26.7% and 51.5% across the two datasets, while strong regression performance is retained with $R^2=0.993$. These results establish persistent topology as an effective inductive bias for representation learning of complex three-dimensional mechanical metamaterials.
item.dc:creator: Songlin Duan, Shuo Yang, Yujia Zheng, Tobin Filleter

item.title: Temporal Specification Guidance for Text-to-Video Generation
item.description: arXiv:2610.20822v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Text-to-video models often generate the visual concepts requested in natural language prompts but fail to satisfy their intended ordering, timing, and persistence requirements. We propose representing these requirements as specifications in a formal Temporal Logic, and introduce Temporal Specification Guidance (TSG), a training-free inference-time framework that turns temporal specifications into executable objectives for guiding video generation during sampling. TSG scores traces of visual concept evidence using differentiable quantitative semantics and uses the score's gradients to construct a specification-guided denoising direction. We instantiate this framework with video-text attention traces, efficient differentiable scores for Metric Temporal Logic, and gradient-derived attention biases. This instantiation requires neither an external concept classifier nor backpropagation through the video transformer. Its attention-steered forward pass yields a denoising direction that augments classifier-free guidance (CFG). On a benchmark of 220 prompts spanning 11 categories of temporal constraints, including ordered object entry and state transitions, this instantiation improves specification satisfaction accuracy over CFG by 9.5-20 percentage points across five models, with minimal memory overhead. These results demonstrate the potential of temporal specifications and differentiable satisfaction objectives as a flexible interface for controlling video generation.
item.dc:creator: Avishree Khare, Hideki Okamoto, Bardh Hoxha, Georgios Fainekos, Rajeev Alur

item.title: EgoJEPA: Beyond Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos
item.description: arXiv:2610.20904v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Egocentric human videos offer a scalable alternative to costly robot demonstra- tions, yet transferring their manipulation priors to robot control remains chal- lenging. The commonly adopted retargeting-based approaches convert human wrist and finger poses into embodiment-specific action commands through hand- crafted geometric mappings. However, such mappings require meticulous recal- ibration across different embodiments and risk propagating hand-tracking errors into downstream robot control pipelines. To this end, we propose EgoJEPA, a three-stage framework that learns embodiment-agnostic representations from ego- centric human videos without rule-based human-to-robot retargeting: 1) Human- action pre-training learns effect-aware latent actions through JEPA-style visual prediction conditioned on hand-motion differences; 2) Latent-action-based world modeling jointly predicts future visual dynamics and latent actions, which decou- ples human prior pre-training from robot-specific control parameterizations; 3) Embodiment-specific tuning adapts the pretrained model to diverse robots through lightweight action adapters. Experiments on five real-world manipulation tasks across three robot embodiments demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of EgoJEPA. It achieves a 74% average success rate under the out-of-domain evalu- ation, compared with 65% for the retargeting baseline, while reducing cumulative cross-embodiment wall-clock cost by 47.2%, from 743.2 to 392.7 hours.
item.dc:creator: Meng Cao, Can Zhao, Jinjie Wei, Haonan Zhao, Yulong Zhang, Duo Han, Xiaofan Li, Ziwu Song, Rongtao Xu, Ruyi Gan, Hao Wang, Qian Wang, Daolin Ma, Ian Reid, Xiaodan Liang

item.title: Line-Augmented cuVSLAM: Robust Visual Odometry in Low-Texture Environments
item.description: arXiv:2610.20958v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autonomous mobile robots in warehouses and production facilities operate in precisely the environments that defeat point-feature visual odometry: featureless aisles, uniform walls, repetitive racking and specular floors. Such environments are, however, rich in straight-edge structure: rack uprights, door frames, wall junctions and cabinet outlines present high-contrast linear edges stable across wide viewpoint changes. A line-feature extension to cuVSLAM, a CUDA-accelerated visual-SLAM system, is presented that recovers this signal. Lines are parameterised as Pl\"ucker coordinates for geometric transport and as the minimal 4-DOF orthonormal representation of Bartoli and Sturm for optimisation; a Cauchy-robust point-to-line residual with analytic Jacobians is folded directly into cuVSLAM's per-frame Gauss-Newton pose solve, and the same line state is jointly refined in the Schur-complement sliding-window bundle adjustment. An adaptive information weight causes lines to assume more of the estimation burden exactly as point features become scarce, and the extension adds residual blocks to existing solvers rather than introducing a second estimator, reducing exactly to the unmodified point pipeline when disabled. Evaluated in RGB-D mode under SE(3) Umeyama alignment with no scale correction, line features reduce mean absolute trajectory error by 38.5% over the 22 sequences of the TUM RGB-D Freiburg3 collection and by 30.1% over the 8 Replica room and office sequences, where median translation error falls by 38.9% and median rotation error by 66.4%, with zero tracking failures in any configuration tested.
item.dc:creator: Dara Molloy, Terry Wu, Wonju Lee, Abhilash Nand Kumar, David Adley, Conor Ferguson, Hesam Rabeti

item.title: MSP: Modality Self-Play for Training Multimodal LLMs Without Paired Cross-Modal Data
item.description: arXiv:2610.20965v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large multimodal models have achieved remarkable progress by scaling model capacity and training on massive paired multimodal data. However, this paradigm introduces a fundamental bottleneck: aligned multimodal datasets are expensive to curate, difficult to scale across diverse modality combinations, and increasingly constrain further progress. We introduce Modality Self-Play (MSP), a training framework for multimodal foundation models based on proxy-mediated modality composition. Instead of relying on paired cross-modal data, MSP uses anchor-supporting proxy textual descriptions of unseen modalities as semantic bridges during training. Given an observed modality (e.g., image or audio), the model generates proxy descriptions for complementary unseen modalities, which are then encoded and aligned with the observed modality through learned bridges, enabling cross-modal interaction without real paired non-text supervision. Our central hypothesis is that proxy text, combined with contrastively trained pretrained encoders, provides sufficient semantic structure for multimodal composition to emerge. We show that MSP enables zero-shot modality composition: models trained only with a real anchor modality and accompanying proxy descriptions can integrate and reason over multiple modalities at inference time despite never observing real paired non-text data during training. Empirically, MSP achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on multiple multimodal benchmarks. Ablation studies further demonstrate that learned bridges improve alignment, while anchor-supporting proxy descriptions enable effective cross-modal composition. MSP removes the need for real paired non-text (e.g., audio-vision) supervision, while continuing to rely on modality-text pairs, pretrained contrastive encoders, and modality-distribution bridge calibration.
item.dc:creator: Robert Moseley, Md Kaykobad Reza, Ameya Patil, Edward Ayrapetian, Salman Asif

item.title: Do As I Do, Not As I Say: On-Policy Distillation Inherits the Teacher in Vision-Language Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.20989v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Improving the reasoning capabilities of vision-language models (VLMs) often relies on post-training with supervision from stronger models. Two common strategies are supervised fine-tuning (SFT), which trains on teacher-generated demonstrations, and on-policy distillation (OPD), which provides teacher feedback on trajectories generated by the student itself. While OPD can be more data-efficient by supervising student-generated trajectories, it is unclear how the teacher's supervision at each state affects the student's learned behavior. To study this question, we conduct a controlled comparison of OPD and filtered SFT across data budgets and tasks where the teacher exhibits different levels of reliability, and analyze how these differences shape student accuracy and completion behavior. Across the two tasks, we find that OPD is effective only when the teacher remains reliable on student-generated trajectories. On ChartQA, where the teacher completes 99% of its solutions, OPD trained on only 10% of the data comes within 1.4 accuracy points of full-data SFT. In contrast, on Geometry3K, where the teacher fails to complete 22% of its solutions, OPD underperforms SFT by 7.9 points, with most of the gap explained by incomplete responses. More strikingly, starting OPD from an SFT student reduces its completion rate from 76% to 62%, effectively erasing the completion behavior learned through SFT. Filtering teacher demonstrations for completeness alone recovers much of SFT's advantage. These results show that on-policy supervision can transfer not only teacher knowledge but also persistent failure modes on student-visited states. Code is available at https://github.com/ffy208/opd-inherits-teacher-vlm.
item.dc:creator: Frank F. Yang, Kefei Yan, Yiren Wang, Yiyang Wang

item.title: SIEVE: Overcoming Topological Obstruction in Equivariant Self-Supervised Learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.21087v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We identify a theoretical incompatibility between 3D point cloud masked autoencoding and SE(3)-equivariant networks. We prove that standard masking triggers a topological collapse, effectively forcing the model to hallucinate orientation without a reference frame. To resolve this, we introduce SIEVE (Scalar Invariant Extraction Via Equivariance), an SE(3)-equivariant self-supervised framework that compresses point cloud geometry into invariant scalar embeddings. At its core is the spherical projection mask, which preserves global pose while obfuscating local semantics, sidestepping the obstruction by construction. Experiments confirm that SIEVE circumvents the predicted collapse where constant and noise masks fail. On downstream point cloud tasks, the resulting embeddings improve over coordinate-based baselines and hand-crafted geometric descriptors, with the largest gains on generalization to unseen shape categories.
item.dc:creator: Jongann Lee, Sun Woo Park, Yun Young Choi

item.title: Spectral-Spatial Interpretation
item.description: arXiv:2610.21114v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Post-hoc image explanations usually show where a model looks using spatial heatmaps or indicate which channels matter using global channel scores. These separate views are limiting for multispectral data because channel relevance is often spatially localized and physically meaningful. We introduce Spectral-Spatial Interpretation (SSI), a full-grid attribution method over position-channel players (g,c). For each spatial position, SSI fixes the observed surrounding context, defines a conditional game over the channels at that position, and applies the Shapley value to this local game. The result is a full spectral-spatial attribution matrix rather than a single heatmap or a global channel ranking. SSI has a clear local interpretation. It satisfies Shapley fairness within each position, and aggregating its channel attributions exactly recovers the position-level contextual contrast obtained by replacing that position with the baseline. SSI also differs from context-averaged Owen-style hierarchical accounting, which uses the same position-channel grouping but averages over external spatial coalitions. On HLS Burn Scar, SSI outperforms an MC-Owen estimator across retained attribution metrics while using only about 6% of its evaluation budget. Across CUB-200, EuroSAT, and HLS Burn Scar under both per-channel mean and zero baselines, SSI achieves the best joint deletion and insertion AUC over dense, flat, and rank-1 baselines, yields the strongest spectral hit rates and channel deletion, and leads spatial localization on both annotated datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/AtheavenMa/Spectral-Spatial-Interpretation.
item.dc:creator: Haotian Ma, Ruqi Yang, Philip Townsend

item.title: ResStreamGS: Residual-Sensitive Dual-Stream Gaussian Splatting for Mobile Volumetric Video Streaming
item.description: arXiv:2610.21121v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Real-time mobile volumetric video enables immersive free-viewpoint experiences, but delivering high-quality 3D content under constrained bandwidth and computation remains challenging. Recent 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) systems, such as V$^3$, enable efficient mobile streaming by encoding time-varying Gaussian attributes with commodity video codecs and hardware decoding. However, existing pipelines treat all Gaussians as frame-varying signals, which is poorly suited to full-scene content where large portions remain temporally stable. Our empirical study shows that frame-wise adaptation and video coding of all Gaussians cause quality degradation in complex full-scene content, particularly in temporally stable regions. To address this issue, we propose ResStreamGS, a residual-sensitive dual-stream framework that processes Gaussians according to their temporal behavior. ResStreamGS identifies residual-sensitive primitives through lightweight probe adaptation and reuses stable Gaussians within each Group of Pictures (GOP). Stable Gaussians are transmitted once per GOP, while only residual-sensitive Gaussians remain in the frame-wise hardware-decodable video stream. Experiments on complex full-scene volumetric videos show that ResStreamGS improves post-codec PSNR by 7.51--8.35~dB over a controlled V$^3$-style all-Gaussians baseline, reduces amortized payload by up to 56.5%, and achieves 30.883~FPS on a Qualcomm Snapdragon 778G platform.
item.dc:creator: Haoran Liu, Di Wu, Wang Luo, Hengyuan Na, Miao Hu, Guocong Quan

item.title: Monotone Piecewise-Linear Harmonization of Multitemporal Multispectral Surface Reflectance With Unsupervised Deep Multiview Pseudoinvariant Features Learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.21183v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Surface reflectance products derived from optical satellite may exhibit systematic inconsistencies across acquisition dates, because atmospheric correction is generally performed independently for each image. Such residual biases distort the temporal behavior of invariant ground targets and reduce the reliability of multitemporal surface reflectance analysis. This study proposes Deep Multitemporal Generalized Canonical Correlation Analysis (DeepMGCCA), an unsupervised deep multiview pseudoinvariant feature learning framework that integrates Deep Generalized Canonical Correlation Analysis (GCCA) with Multivariate Alteration Detection (MAD) to identify deep-pseudoinvariant features (DIFs) for the removal of surface reflectance biases across multitemporal satellite observations. Unlike conventional MAD-based approaches that rely on linear GCCA, the proposed framework replaces date-specific linear projections with a shared convolutional encoder. The framework learns deep invariant features (DIFs) directly from pixel-weighted canonical variates via iterative reweighting strategy, while a reconstruction regularizer preserves surface reflectance information and prevents degenerate collapse from suppressing genuine temporal variability. Experiments were conducted on four annual Landsat-8/9 and Sentinel-2 acquisitions across four regions of interest (ROIs) to evaluate four DIF-based harmonization transforms. A monotone piecewise-linear transform derived from DIFs quantiles consistently achieved the largest bias reduction, lowering the between-date spectral angle by up to 2.54 and RMSE by 0.015, and raising PSNR by up to 4.04~dB. These findings demonstrate the potential of deep invariant feature learning for multitemporal surface reflectance bias removal while highlighting the importance of preserving physically meaningful temporal and spectral information during nonlinear representation learning.
item.dc:creator: Lino Garda Denaro, Chia-Hsiang Lin

item.title: LICOA: Learning Instruction-Conditioned Optical Actions for Mobile Spatial Augmented Reality
item.description: arXiv:2610.21282v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spatial augmented reality (SAR) augments physical environments with projected content, but most systems assume that the projector pose, target region, or motion path has been fixed or specified. We instead make projected light an embodied action: given a language instruction and current visual observations, a system must decide how to move and where and at what scale to place the projection. We introduce LICOA to realize this capability. Its differential-drive chassis provides room-scale approach and repositioning, while a steerable mirror with two degrees of freedom (2DoF) and projection scale provide rapid local control of the beam. A shared interface maps synchronized external and onboard RGB cameras with robot control state to physical optical actions across pretrained action models. Because instruction-conditioned optical action lacks dedicated training data and a common evaluation protocol, we construct a matched simulation embodiment and a corpus with 150 tasks and 7,500 rendered episodes, then evaluate models trained only on this corpus in previously unseen real-world environments. Across 480 complete closed-loop real-world execution trials (rollouts) on 12 tasks, the best adapted action model achieves a 57.50% success rate and 40.64% success weighted by path length, compared with 8.33% and 5.15% for the same architecture trained from scratch. A further 150 real-world ablation rollouts support the need for both camera views and coordinated control of the chassis and mirror. These results establish a physical platform, shared perception and optical action interface, corpus, and real-world evaluation protocol for treating projected light as an embodied action.
item.dc:creator: Yuchen Deng, Shunkai Zhou, Ruixuan Zhu, Haibin Ling, Bingyao Huang

item.title: Mallea: Building, Steering, and Memorizing Worlds with Coding Agent
item.description: arXiv:2610.21283v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Code world models represent world dynamics through explicit state and executable rules. We investigate how to coordinate object representations, behavioral revisions, and visual memory within this formulation. We present Mallea, a system for building, steering, and memorizing worlds from text. A coding agent infers object interaction requirements from the prompt and jointly plans object structure, properties, and rules, favoring compact representations that support those requirements. The world evolves under the planned rules; optional user actions steer it, while text requests can edit properties or extend capabilities with unaffected state preserved. Object texture memory retains reusable appearance only for whitebox-defined objects and adapts it as those objects change. The program advances world state, while a generative renderer combines current structure with remembered appearance. By organizing construction, intervention, and memory around the same objects, Mallea conditions subsequent observations on the latest state and compatible appearance. Project page: https://lxycopper.github.io/Mallea.
item.dc:creator: Xuanyi Liu, Ruiqi Li, Siwei Ma

item.title: DocPilot: Interactive Agent Orchestration and Training for Long Visual Document Understanding
item.description: arXiv:2610.21327v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal long-document question answering requires models to seek sparse evidence across pages and modalities, understand heterogeneous document content, and reason over the collected evidence. Even advanced vision-language models (VLMs) can overlook sparse evidence and struggle with cross-modal reasoning in a single pass. Existing document agents further introduce multi-step interaction, but some still rely on predefined workflows or coarse-grained actions, limiting the flexibility and granularity of document reasoning. We introduce DocPilot, an agentic document framework that supports expressive orchestration and makes complex document solving learnable by small language models (SLMs). DocPilot orchestrates evidence seeking through page-level navigation and fine-grained evidence localization, and integrates local visual inspection, code-based numerical reasoning, and cross-modal reasoning for multimodal understanding. To transfer these capabilities to small models, we propose curriculum-based agentic training that progresses from single-ability learning to adaptive orchestration through supervision from data-grounded reasoning traces and executable interaction trajectories. Across MMLongBench-Doc, DocBench, FinRAGBench-V, and MADQA, DocPilot achieves strong gains with frontier VLM backbones, while DocPilot-4B delivers competitive performance against substantially larger models, demonstrating strong effectiveness and generalization across diverse long-document reasoning settings. The code is available at https://github.com/HKUSTDial/DocPilot.
item.dc:creator: Zhuowen Liang, Xiaotian Lin, Yuyu Luo, Haixun Wang, Nan Tang

item.title: X-Fly: Learning to Reach and Stop in Full-Chunk Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
item.description: arXiv:2610.21450v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Aerial vision-language navigation (VLN) agents built on large vision-language models are expensive to query. Executing a complete predicted action chunk before replanning amortizes this cost, reducing model inference from 195 to 42 ms per executed waypoint for our policy. It also moves the states at which the policy is queried away from expert demonstrations, which supervise neither recovery from these states nor termination at the learner's own arrival. On OpenFly test-seen, no-stop failures account for 47.78% of full-chunk behavior cloning (BC) outcomes. We present X-Fly, a staged training framework for full-chunk aerial VLN. Recovery DAgger labels learner-visited decision states with smooth chunks that reconnect to future expert segments and with STOP at the first in-region state. Flow-GRPO then jointly refines the chunked flow controller and a Bernoulli STOP policy from same-task closed-loop outcomes, supplemented by outcome-verified stopping supervision. With eight controls per decision, X-Fly reaches 74.18% SR on test-seen and 51.73% on test-unseen, compared with 16.45% and 18.43% for full-chunk BC and 32.04% and 29.46% for DreamFly.
item.dc:creator: Ruibin Ju, Ruifeng Cai, Min Xu, Lin Wang

item.title: Full-Duplex Interaction with Speech, Expressions and Gestures
item.description: arXiv:2610.21452v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Human face-to-face conversation requires coordinating speech, gestures and expressions across both speaking and listening. We present ELLSA 2, an end-to-end full-duplex dialogue model that jointly optimizes speech interaction and streaming gesture-expression generation. An autoregressive, chunk-wise synthesizer combines pretrained acoustic features with distinct listening and speaking hidden states from the dialogue backbone and speech synthesizer, enabling continuous non-verbal generation even when the model is verbally silent. To translate dialogue understanding into vivid semantic gestures, we introduce contextual semantic calls and template guidance, separating whether to invoke an available semantic gesture from how to realize it. We also establish a curated data and evaluation pipeline for dialog-aware co-speech gesture generation and investigate reference-based multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as automatic judges. Experiments show that ELLSA 2 remains highly competitive with open-source full-duplex speech interaction models and outperforms cascaded baselines across dialog-aware gesture and expression metrics. Semantic template guidance further significantly improves semantic gesture quality. Strong system-level correlations with human judgments support these reference-based scores as useful preliminary metrics for full-duplex and semantic gesture assessment. Together, these results advance dialogue modeling from spoken responses toward coordinated multimodal interaction.
item.dc:creator: Siyin Wang, Wenyi Yu, Terumi Chiba, Xianzhao Chen, Xiaohai Tian, Jun Zhang, Lu Lu, Chao Zhang

item.title: CarryOn: A Dual-Loop Harness for Personalized and Reliable Robot Assistance
item.description: arXiv:2610.21453v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While generalist vision-language-action (VLA) models have enabled diverse open-world manipulation, real-world robotic assistance requires two critical capabilities they currently lack: personalization and reliable execution. First, executing an instruction like "make me a sandwich" requires grounding subtask decomposition in persistent user preferences rather than relying on a single generic solution. Second, reliable deployment demands explainable safety assurance that proactively prevents hazards and gracefully recovers from occasional physical failures. To address these gaps, we present CarryOn, a dual-loop harness designed to augment a frozen VLA policy. The planning loop maintains persistent user-level and scene-level context that is continually grounded against new observations and revised through interaction, enabling personalized task selection and execution grounding across conversations and changing scenes. The execution loop actively supervises policy rollouts, shielding actions from predicted hazardous contact. When execution fails, the system invokes reusable control-based recovery skills that restore task progress and are refined through reflection on earlier failures. On a real robot and in simulation, CarryOn dispatches preference-consistent subtasks across users and scenes, reduces the violation rate of an already safety-finetuned VLA from 52.6% to 6.1%, and increases recovery success from 13% to 80% when refined skills are reused.
item.dc:creator: Zixuan Wang, Yuqi Liu, Yuxin Chen, Sengqiao Yang, Jinhui Ye, Pengguang Chen, Changsheng Lu, Shu Liu, Bei Yu, Jiaya Jia

item.title: AI-Driven Disaster Response and Displacement Monitoring
item.description: arXiv:2610.21482v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) has demonstrated its potential across a wide range of humanitarian tasks, offering scalable and data-driven solutions to some of the world's most pressing challenges. For instance, in addressing climate change, AI-powered models are being used for faster and more accurate global weather forecasting, control and design of renewable energy, and monitoring deforestation. Machine learning algorithms analyze satellite imagery and socioeconomic data to predict poverty and promote sustainable development. AI has also transformed disaster response and conflict monitoring, providing innovative solutions for assessing damage and urgent needs and tracking displacement.
item.dc:creator: Noora Al-Emadi, Muhammad Imran, Yin Yang, Ingmar Weber, Fabjan Lashi, Gaia Rigodanza, Ivana Hajzmanova, Ferda Ofli

item.title: Training-Free Target-Aware Refinement of 3D Gaussian Language Map
item.description: arXiv:2610.21619v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Distilling vision-language features into 3D Gaussian Splatting yields a language map that can be queried with arbitrary text. In deployment, however, a small set of user-specified targets must be reliably located, which current distilled maps often miss, while open-vocabulary queryability for other words must remain intact. We propose a training-free, target-aware refinement of an already-distilled language map. Guided by a text-promptable segmenter, the visual embedding inside each detected target region is blended with the target text embedding, a convex combination whose coefficient sets the amount of injected prior, while non-target regions are left untouched. Injecting too much overwrites appearance cues and general queryability, so we seek, for each target, the smallest coefficient that still lets it win, and we obtain every coefficient in closed form, leaving no hyperparameters to tune. We further identify a failure mode of injection in language-goal localization. Text embeddings share a common component, and injecting them makes the standard cosine read-out query-agnostic, which a centering step in the read-out removes. Across three benchmarks, the refinement consistently improves open-vocabulary segmentation, roughly doubling the base mIoU on Replica, and localizes language goals more reliably than the base map. It also transfers as a plug-in to off-the-shelf field-based and object-level language maps and supports a real-world demonstration in which a legged robot navigates to natural-language goals. Project page and code: https://lab-of-ai-and-robotics.github.io/target-aware-langmap/
item.dc:creator: Sibaek Lee, Kyeongsu Kang, Seongbo Ha, Yewon Jeon, Joonyeol Choi, Daegeol Ko, Jaehyuk Hur, Taemin Choi, Minsu Kim, Hyungjoo Ahn, Wonsok Yoo, Hyeonwoo Yu

item.title: From Sketch to Scene: Relightable Garment Reconstruction from Marked Sketches
item.description: arXiv:2610.21865v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sketching is one of the most natural ways for people to express visual ideas. Unlike the text prompts that most generative systems rely on today, a sketch captures spatial structure and intent directly, including where a designer wants highlights and shadows to appear. Yet current sketch-to-3D pipelines have no input for that intent: they bake the drawn shading into the texture as dark paint, and the light cannot be moved. We propose a system that transforms a rough garment sketch, marked with sparse annotations (a star for a highlight and a moon for a shadow), and a short text prompt describing the texture, into a textured 3D mesh with an explicit directional light, as a scene that can be relit and edited after generation. The two symbols are the most frequent proposals in an elicitation study with art students. From the marked sketch the system predicts the scene's directional light and, separately, a displacement field that bends the surface so that the moon-marked regions fall into shadow under that light, rather than being painted dark in the texture.
item.dc:creator: Ahmet Ne\c{c}irvan Do\u{g}an, Eren Acar Ba\c{s}aran, Metin Sezgin, Zahra Montazeri

item.title: Following Delegation Traces to Study Human Oversight in Interaction with Multimodal AI
item.description: arXiv:2610.21948v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As multimodal AI systems are becoming our everyday thought partners, the shift towards studying how users transfer control to these systems becomes especially urgent. In this paper, we report an overview of findings from an online study with n=56 AI-literate participants and 392 Video Question Answering trials. After inspecting each multimodal AI response, participants rated task-specific trust and selected one of three intended policies for an analogous future task: reject AI assistance, use it with verification, or delegate fully to the AI. Within participants, post-interaction trust strongly predicted the user's delegation choices (OR=14.97, 95% CI [7.14,31.37]). Trust and delegation nevertheless remained distinct. Verification was the dominant policy and often co-occurred with high trust. Delegation also increased with task order after adjustment for momentary and participant-level trust (OR=1.22, 95% CI [1.02,1.45]), indicating an experience-related component that self-reported trust ratings alone could not capture. These findings motivate a shift from intended delegation to a non-intrusive observation of how delegation is enacted in collaborative human-AI tasks. We therefore conclude by proposing enacted delegation traces as a methodological framework for future studies of multimodal and agentic AI use.
item.dc:creator: Agnese Chiatti, Matteo Matteucci, Viola Schiaffonati

item.title: P2TPO: Structure-Aligned Page-to-Token Credit Assignment for Full-Page Document Parsing
item.description: arXiv:2610.21979v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: End-to-end full-page document parsing must preserve the content and structure of heterogeneous elements, yet otherwise accurate outputs can contain local errors and omissions. A single page-level advantage does not explicitly identify which elements differ in quality across sampled outputs or where their errors occur. We introduce Page-to-Token Policy Optimization (P2TPO), a structure-aligned credit-assignment framework that operates on full-page policy trajectories. Reference-element alignment first associates block-level quality contrasts with generated spans. Unified Anchor Pricing (UAP) incorporates matched and missing element outcomes and provides feedback relative to a fixed quality ceiling when sampled outputs receive identical but imperfect scores for a reference element. Within matched blocks, Span Credit Redistribution (SCR) redistributes existing block credit according to aligned correct and erroneous spans, using boundary proxies for within-block omissions while preserving the total block-derived advantage across its tokens. Under a fixed-weight additive page utility, we show that element-indexed contrasts retain local quality differences that page-level aggregation can cancel out. In the main experimental comparison, P2TPO outperforms all evaluated policy optimization baselines in seed-averaged scores on each of the six document parsing benchmarks. Additional experiments demonstrate gains across model scales and initializations.
item.dc:creator: Yong Zu, Ninghua Yang, Zezhong Tan, Xinhong Ma, Ziqiang Dong, Yang Yang

item.title: GRID-Planner: Graph-Structured Relational Reward Shaping for Diffusion Planning
item.description: arXiv:2610.21984v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autonomous driving planning requires selecting trajectories that remain safe, rule-compliant, and comfortable under complex multi-agent interactions, yet robust closed-loop decision making in planning-critical scenes remains challenging. Existing diffusion- and RL-based planners often rely on generic rewards and use relational structure mainly for representation, limiting how planning-critical rollouts shape policy improvement. We present GRID-Planner, a graph--reward integrated diffusion planning framework that aligns generative planning with structured relational signals. Specifically, GRID-Planner combines graph-aware importance weighting, a time-indexed relational reward surrogate, and an advantage-weighted diffusion objective with on-policy self-distillation, forming a rollout-return-advantage-update loop without explicit likelihoods. Experiments on nuPlan and interPlan show that, compared with the diffusion-only baseline, GRID-Planner reduces collision rate, lane deviation, and jerk by 35.8\%, 60.8\%, and 27.4\%, respectively, and improves the planning score by 3.4\%. Project website: https://github.com/yangzhaojason/GRID-Planner.
item.dc:creator: Zhao Yang, Zezhong Qian, Yinan Shi, Longjun Liu, Yawei Jueluo

item.title: REKI: Registering Knowledge in VLAs
item.description: arXiv:2610.22178v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce REKI, a 2.4B vision-language-action model (VLA) pretrained exclusively on public data that sets a new Pareto frontier between performance and model size: on LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin Clean2Rand and RoboCasa365, it is outperformed only by models about twice its size. REKI consists of a vision-language model (VLM) followed by a flow-matching action expert, and is pretrained on a curated mixture of public robot, egocentric human and vision-language data. Additionally, we endow it with a memory that gives the policy access to its recent past at negligible cost: a few register tokens in the action expert summarise the output of the VLM at each frame and persist in the expert's cache. This memory improves success in simulation and on real robots, and makes oscillations between poses about four times rarer. REKI uses a simple model design and training paradigm, and is optimised to be efficient at training and inference. We release the full code across data curation, training, inference and evaluation, deployment, and all pretrained and finetuned model weights: https://github.com/kyutai-labs/reki.
item.dc:creator: Juliette Marrie, Paul Pacaud, Adrien Ramanana Rahary, Shizhe Chen, Moritz B\"ohle

item.title: OS-Helix: Unifying GUI Interaction and Code Execution in Native Computer-Using Agents
item.description: arXiv:2610.22234v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Real desktop automation is neither purely visual nor purely programmatic. Agents must understand user-facing interfaces while efficiently manipulating files, scripts, and system state. However, native GUI/code coordination cannot be obtained by prompt-level tool composition. In our preliminary experiments, naively adding a code tool degrades a GUI agent, revealing that GUI/code routing must be internalized through training on high-quality hybrid data. We present OS-Helix, an end-to-end trained multimodal computer-using agent that unifies GUI actions and code execution in one action space. To construct the required supervision, we introduce application-artifact composition, pairing desktop applications with authentic file artifacts to instantiate executable Ubuntu states, and a decoupled instruction/evaluator generation pipeline that produces environment-grounded tasks whose final states can be verified regardless of the solution modality. We cold-start the policy with SFT on filtered hybrid data and further improve it through online RL in live desktop environments. For RL, we propose Step-balanced GSPO, which aggregates importance weight by action step rather than raw assistant tokens to prevent long code actions from dominating heterogeneous-action optimization. On OSWorld-Verified, OS-Helix-27B and OS-Helix-35B-A3B achieve relative improvements of 35.0% and 33.7% over their matched Qwen3.5 hybrid baselines, while OS-Helix-27B-RL further improves by 42.9% to reach 66.44% success. Ablations provide evidence consistent with contributions from learned GUI/code coordination, scalable verifiable supervision, and action step balanced optimization, while demonstrating cross-platform transfer on WindowsAgentArena. Our project homepage is at https://os-copilot.github.io/OS-Helix/.
item.dc:creator: Bowen Yang, Kaiming Jin, Zichen Ding, Zhenyu Wu, Zehao Li, Zhoumianze Liu, Kanzhi Cheng, Fangzhi Xu, Yanan Sun, Qiushi Sun, Yu Qiao

item.title: Denoising Textures is a Different Ballgame Altogether!
item.description: arXiv:2610.22258v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The human brain effortlessly deciphers colors and textures from visual stimuli and reconstructs the world around us, yet preserving such details remains challenging in image denoising. While significant progress has been made in generic image denoising, the problem of texture denoising has remained relatively under-explored. Fine details, such as intricate patterns and repetitive structures, often suffer from over-smoothing even in deep learning based approaches for denoising. In this paper, we analyze the behavior of state-of-the-art (SOTA) denoisers on texture datasets and show that performance improvements are possible only by fine-tuning the denoisers on the texture datasets. Surprisingly, fine-tuning on texture datasets result in the models catastrophically forgetting the original dataset. These findings highlight the need for specialized treatment of textures in denoising. Since denoising quality directly impacts downstream tasks such as generative modelling, we argue that dedicated texture aware denoisers are essential for faithful texture reconstruction and synthesis.
item.dc:creator: Saptarshi Mandal, Oindrila Haldar, Chirayata Bhattacharya, Chandra Sekhar Seelamantula, Zhiwei Xu, Thrasyvoulos N. Pappas, Gaurav Sharma

item.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.22364v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Predicting how the world responds to an action requires more than what can be seen: robots must account for environmental factors that are neither directly observable nor explicitly specified, from physical properties such as friction and mass to human-defined environmental rules. We introduce T2-Z for test-time optimization of environment latents, which augments a robotic world model with a learnable environment latent to condition world predictions. This compact latent captures underlying environmental variation without supervision of what environmental factors exist or what values they take. During training, T2-Z alternates between two stages: a world-model optimization stage that fixes the latents and learns general action-conditioned dynamics across environments; and an environment-latent optimization stage that freezes the world model and optimizes the conditioning latents, allowing latent structure to emerge purely through world prediction. At test time, the world model remains frozen and a newly initialized environment latent is optimized from one or more test-time interactions, adapting the model to previously unseen environmental configurations. Across 7 simulated settings and 4 real-world robotic tasks, T2-Z reduces object prediction error metric from 15.20 to 7.00 and raises action success from 33.73% to 72.96%. Its emergent latents capture structured representations of individual and compounded factors across diverse visual scenes. Ablations further show that T2-Z can efficiently infer environment latents from as little as a single test-time interaction trajectory.
item.dc:creator: Chenyuan Zhou, Yining Hong, Huang Huang, Yunfan Jiang, Wenlong Huang, David Held, Vitor Campagnolo Guizilini, Yue Wang, Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu, Leonidas Guibas, Yejin Choi

item.title: InkSight: Offline-to-Online Handwriting Conversion by Teaching Vision-Language Models to Read and Write
item.description: arXiv:2402.05804v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Digital note-taking is gaining popularity, offering a durable, editable, and easily indexable way of storing notes in a vectorized form, known as digital ink. However, a substantial gap remains between this way of note-taking and traditional pen-and-paper note-taking, a practice that is still favored by a vast majority. Our work InkSight, aims to bridge the gap by empowering physical note-takers to effortlessly convert their work (offline handwriting) to digital ink (online handwriting), a process we refer to as derendering. Prior research on the topic has focused on the geometric properties of images, resulting in limited generalization beyond their training domains. Our approach combines reading and writing priors, allowing training a model in the absence of large amounts of paired samples, which are difficult to obtain. To our knowledge, this is the first work that effectively derenders handwritten text in arbitrary photos with diverse visual characteristics and backgrounds. Furthermore, it generalizes beyond its training domain into simple sketches. Our human evaluation reveals that 87% of the samples produced by our model on the challenging HierText dataset are considered as a valid tracing of the input image and 67% look like a pen trajectory traced by a human.
item.dc:creator: Blagoj Mitrevski, Arina Rak, Julian Schnitzler, Chengkun Li, Andrii Maksai, Jesse Berent, Claudiu Musat

item.title: Text-to-Image Synthesis: A Decade Survey
item.description: arXiv:2411.16164v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Text-to-image synthesis (T2I) focuses on generating high-quality images from textual descriptions In this survey, we review 490 papers on T2I spanning the past decade, with representative advances covered through 2026. We start by briefly introducing how GANs, autoregressive models, and diffusion models have been used for image generation, and we additionally examine the shared components whose evolution has driven recent progress. Building on this foundation, we discuss the development of these models for T2I and organize cutting-edge research by problem rather than by chronology alone, covering controllability, personalized and identity-preserving generation, instruction-based image editing, preference alignment and post-training with human and AI feedback, efficiency, safety, and consistency in content and spatial relationships. We further review unified multimodal understanding-and-generation models, summarize the datasets and evaluation metrics commonly used in T2I research, and provide a comparative discussion of the three paradigms together with their respective trade-offs. Finally, we discuss the potential applications of T2I within AIGC, along with the challenges and forward-looking research opportunities in this field.
item.dc:creator: Nonghai Zhang, Hao Tang

item.title: Towards Accurate State Estimation: Motion Dynamics Kalman Filter for 3D Multi-Object Tracking
item.description: arXiv:2505.07254v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Robust 3D state estimation in multi-object tracking is crucial for object localization in self-driving vehicles. Misalignment between the Kalman filter (KF) motion model and an object's motion can cause state drift, particularly in distant and occlusion cases. The static motion model assumption in the conventional KF is widely used in 3D MOT due to its low latency; however, its estimation accuracy degrades as the object's motion disaligns with the chosen model due to traffic. Although recent work introduces a multimodel KF that runs multiple motion models simultaneously to improve state robustness, it incurs significant computational overhead, so many studies still favor the constant-motion KF to maintain efficiency. This work addresses this trade-off by introducing a motion dynamics Kalman filter (MD-KF) that accounts for motion variation through temporal modeling of object motion and adaptively scales the contribution of the motion components in the motion model to correct state-prediction drift caused by this variation, while maintaining computational efficiency by retaining a single-model structure. Evaluations on KITTI and the Waymo Open Dataset, complemented by vehicle experiments, show that MD-KF achieves tracking performance comparable to multimodel KF with an average 1.72x speedup, while outperforming it in handling highly distant and prolonged occluded objects.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Nagy, Naoufel Werghi, Bilal Hassan, Jorge Dias, Majid Khonji

item.title: RUSplatting: Robust 3D Gaussian Splatting for Sparse-View Underwater Scene Reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2505.15737v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reconstructing high-fidelity underwater scenes remains a challenging task due to light absorption, scattering, and limited visibility inherent in aquatic environments. This paper presents an enhanced Gaussian Splatting-based framework that improves both the visual quality and geometric accuracy of deep underwater rendering. We propose decoupled learning for RGB channels, guided by the physics of underwater attenuation, to enable more accurate colour restoration. To address sparse-view limitations and improve view consistency, we introduce a frame interpolation strategy with a novel adaptive weighting scheme. Additionally, we introduce a new loss function aimed at reducing noise while preserving edges, which is essential for deep-sea content. We also release a newly collected dataset, Submerged3D, captured specifically in deep-sea environments. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods with PSNR gains up to 1.90dB, delivering superior perceptual quality and robustness, and offering promising directions for marine robotics and underwater visual analytics. The code of RUSplatting is available at https://github.com/theflash987/RUSplatting and the dataset Submerged3D can be downloaded at https://zenodo.org/records/15482420.
item.dc:creator: Zhuodong Jiang, Haoran Wang, Guoxi Huang, Brett Seymour, Nantheera Anantrasirichai

item.title: HonestFace: Towards Honest Face Restoration with One-Step Diffusion Model
item.description: arXiv:2505.18469v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Face restoration has achieved significant advancements through the years of development. However, maintaining high fidelity and authenticity while avoiding artifacts remains challenging, especially in extreme degradation scenarios. This highlights the need for models that are more ``honest'' in their reconstruction from low-quality inputs, accurately reflecting original characteristics. In this work, we propose HonestFace, a novel approach for honest face restoration with identity consistency and realistic textures. To achieve this, HonestFace incorporates several key components. First, we propose an identity embedder to effectively capture and preserve crucial identity features from both the low-quality input and multiple reference faces. Second, a masked face alignment method is presented to enhance fine-grained details and textural authenticity. Furthermore, we present a new real-world reference-based face restoration dataset, \textbf{MultiRefCeleb-Test}, with multiple high-quality references and low-quality inputs. Leveraging these contributions within a one-step diffusion model framework, HonestFace delivers excellent restoration results in terms of facial fidelity and realism. Experiments demonstrate that our approach surpasses state-of-the-art methods, achieving superior performance in both visual quality and quantitative assessments. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://github.com/jkwang28/HonestFace .
item.dc:creator: Jingkai Wang, Wu Miao, Jue Gong, Zheng Chen, Xing Liu, Hong Gu, Yutong Liu, Yulun Zhang

item.title: AI Knows Where You Are: Exposure, Bias, and Inference in Multimodal Geolocation with KoreaGEO
item.description: arXiv:2506.03371v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent advances in vision-language models (VLMs) have enabled accurate image-based geolocation, raising serious concerns about location privacy risks in everyday social media posts. Yet, a systematic evaluation of such risks is still lacking: existing benchmarks show coarse granularity, linguistic bias, and a neglect of multimodal privacy risks. To address these gaps, we introduce KoreaGEO, the first fine-grained, multimodal, and privacy-aware benchmark for geolocation, built on Korean street views. The benchmark covers four socio-spatial clusters and nine place types with rich contextual annotations and two captioning styles that simulate real-world privacy exposure. To evaluate mainstream VLMs, we design a three-path protocol spanning image-only, functional-caption, and high-risk-caption inputs, enabling systematic analysis of localization accuracy, spatial bias, and reasoning behavior. Results show that input modality exerts a stronger influence on localization precision and privacy exposure than model scale or architecture, with high-risk captions substantially boosting accuracy. Moreover, they highlight structural prediction biases toward core cities.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
item.dc:creator: Xiaonan Wang, Bo Shao, Hansaem Kim

item.title: UniFGVC: Universal Training-Free Few-Shot Fine-Grained Vision Classification via Attribute-Aware Multimodal Retrieval
item.description: arXiv:2508.04136v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Few-shot fine-grained visual classification (FGVC) aims to discriminate between subtly different categories with very limited data. While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLM) exhibit strong capabilities in both fine-grained visual understanding and open-world category recognition, directly fine-tuning them on few-shot FGVC tasks typically leads to overfitting on sparse samples, which erodes their valuable open-world knowledge and compromises generalization. To fundamentally overcome this limitation, we present UniFGVC, a universal training-free framework that shifts the paradigm from parameter fine-tuning to training-free retrieval-based inference. UniFGVC reframes few-shot FGVC as a multimodal retrieval problem using predefined category templates. Its core is the Category-Discriminative Visual Captioner (CDV-Captioner), an attribute-aware module designed to leverage MLLM for generating structured textual descriptions that explicitly pinpoint discriminative visual attributes between similar classes. By integrating chain-of-thought reasoning and visual references, CDV-Captioner mitigates hallucination and maximizes the discriminative power of textual captions, thereby converting images into attribute-enriched image-description pairs. Subsequently, utilizing arbitrary pre-trained visual and textual encoders in a plug-and-play manner, UniFGVC extracts features from both modalities and computes their similarity with all category templates for recognition. Extensive experiments on 12 FGVC datasets demonstrate UniFGVC's universal compatibility and consistent superiority. It not only outperforms existing few-shot CLIP-based methods but also surpasses several fully-supervised MLLM-based approaches, confirming the general advantage of the proposed retrieval paradigm.
item.dc:creator: Haiyun Guo, Hongyu Guo, Xiangzhao Hao, Jiarui Guo, Jinqiao Wang, Tat-Seng Chua

item.title: Uncovering Grounding IDs: How External Cues Shape Multi-Modal Binding
item.description: arXiv:2509.24072v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) perform well on multimodal tasks, but their ability to reason and precisely align visual and textual information still has room for improvement. In this study, we show that external visual cues, such as symbols or grid lines, help LVLMs form more accurate connections between visual components, such as objects, and their corresponding textual descriptions, improving their grounding and reasoning abilities. We introduce the concept of Grounding IDs, which are latent identifiers that arise within the model as a result of external cues structuring both visual and textual modalities. Our analysis reveals that partition-inducing external cues lead to Grounding IDs that make better alignment between corresponding visual and text representations, helping the model focus on relevant information. We find that Grounding IDs enhance attention between related components, improving cross-modal grounding and reducing hallucinations. Overall, our results show that Grounding IDs are a key mechanism that enables external cues to improve cross-modal alignment, reduce errors, and enhance the overall performance of LVLMs across a range of multimodal tasks.
item.dc:creator: Amirmohammad Izadi, Hosein Hasani, Fatemeh Askari, Mobin Bagherian, Sadegh Mohammadian, Mohammad Izadi, Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah

item.title: Can MLLMs Read the Room? A Multimodal Benchmark for Assessing Deception in Multi-Party Social Interactions
item.description: arXiv:2511.16221v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Despite their advanced reasoning capabilities, state-of-the-art Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) still lack a core component of human intelligence: the ability to "read the room" and assess deception in complex social interactions. To rigorously evaluate this limitation, we introduce Multimodal Interactive Deception Assessment (MIDA), a new task and multimodal dataset comprising synchronized video and text with verifiable ground-truth labels for every statement. We benchmark 12 state-of-the-art open- and closed-source MLLMs and identify a substantial performance gap: even powerful models such as GPT-4o struggle to reliably distinguish truthful statements from deceptive ones. Our analysis shows that current models have difficulty grounding language in multimodal social cues and modeling what others know, believe, or intend. To address these limitations, we propose a Social Chain-of-Thought (SoCoT) reasoning pipeline and a Dynamic Social Epistemic Memory (DSEM) module. Experimental results show that structured epistemic memory consistently improves deception assessment, while multimodal social-cue reasoning remains a challenging and important direction for future research.
item.dc:creator: Caixin Kang, Yifei Huang, Liangyang Ouyang, Mingfang Zhang, Ruicong Liu, Yoichi Sato

item.title: Active Visual Perception: Opportunities and Challenges
item.description: arXiv:2512.03687v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Active visual perception enables an intelligent system to improve perception by controlling how visual evidence is acquired. However, differences in how active perception is defined and evaluated make approaches difficult to compare across tasks. This review clarifies the field's functional scope by distinguishing active observation acquisition from processing fixed inputs. It then organizes representative literature around four questions about what evidence the task requires, which actions can obtain it, how candidate observations should be valued, and how the next sensing action should be selected and executed. New observations update the perceptual state and guide subsequent decisions, forming a closed loop. To evaluate the benefits of active perception, the review examines datasets, interactive environments, physical platforms, and baseline comparisons, and develops an evaluation framework linking improvements in visual evidence to downstream task outcomes while accounting for acquisition costs and risks. The analysis concludes that predicted observation value does not guarantee that useful evidence can be acquired through feasible actions, while task success alone cannot establish the benefit of active observation selection. Further progress requires reliable value estimation and planning over longer decision sequences under physical and resource constraints. It also requires grounding semantic reasoning in acquired evidence and maintaining effective collaboration under imperfect communication, with these capabilities verified through reproducible evaluation of the complete perception and action loop.
item.dc:creator: Yian Li, Xiaoyu Guo, Hao Zhang, Jiayu Chen, Shuiwang Li, Xiaowei Dai

item.title: VDE Bench: Evaluating The Capability of Image Editing Models to Modify Visual Documents
item.description: arXiv:2602.00122v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Image editing models can modify visual content through natural language, but editing dense documents requires precise local changes amid tightly coupled text, tables, and layout. We introduce VDE Bench, an evaluation resource for studying instruction-guided editing of Chinese and English document images. VDE Bench contains 3,506 instruction-guided image editing samples, including 1,578 text-region edits and 1,928 table-region edits. The benchmark pairs editing instructions and reference images with annotated editing regions and structured OCR outputs. Its evaluation protocol combines region-level and full-page measurements to assess textual correctness, structural fidelity, and visual content preservation. By focusing on the interaction between local edits and their surrounding document context, VDE Bench complements existing visual text editing benchmarks and provides a resource for diagnosing document-specific editing failures.
item.dc:creator: Hongzhu Yi, Yujia Yang, Yuanxiang Wang, Tong Li, Zhenyu Guan, Tianyu Zong, Jiahuan Chen, Chenxi Bao, Tiankun Yang, Haopeng Jin, Yixuan Yuan, Xinming Wang, Tao Yu, Ruilin Gao, Ruiwen Tao, Haijin Liang, Jin Ma, Jinwen Luo, Yeshani, Xinyu Zuo, Jungang Xu

item.title: ReText: Text Boosts Generalization in Image-Based Person Re-identification
item.description: arXiv:2602.05785v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Generalizable image-based person re-identification (Re-ID) aims to recognize individuals across cameras in unseen domains without retraining. While visual features are sensitive to domain shifts, natural language descriptions remain consistent across domains, regardless of lighting changes and other biases. Since well-known multi-camera datasets lack textual descriptions, we update them with captions through a fine-tuned Vision-Language Model (VLM). We propose ReText, a novel method trained with textual supervision to enrich visual features with semantic cues. Besides, inspired by recent findings showing that incorporating single-camera data into training improves generalization, we also adopt this strategy. However, in contrast to such prior works, we exploit not only visual information but also the textual annotations naturally accompanying these samples. Finally, during training, ReText jointly optimizes three tasks: (1) Re-ID, (2) image-text matching, and (3) image reconstruction guided by text. Experiments demonstrate that ReText achieves strong generalization and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on cross-domain Re-ID benchmarks. The expanded multi-camera datasets and VLM weights are publicly available at https://github.com/timmzak/ReText.
item.dc:creator: Timur Mamedov, Karina Kvanchiani, Anton Konushin, Vadim Konushin

item.title: SceneReVis: A Self-Reflective Vision-Grounded Framework for 3D Indoor Scene Synthesis via Multi-Turn RL
item.description: arXiv:2602.09432v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Current one-pass 3D scene synthesis methods often suffer from spatial hallucinations, such as collisions, due to a lack of deliberative reasoning. To bridge this gap, we introduce SceneReVis, a vision-grounded self-reflection framework that employs an iterative "diagnose-and-act" loop to explicitly intercept and resolve spatial conflicts using multi-modal feedback. To support this step-wise paradigm, we construct SceneChain-12k, a large-scale dataset of causal construction trajectories derived through a novel reverse engineering pipeline. We further propose a two-stage training recipe that transitions from Supervised Fine-Tuning to Agentic Reinforcement Learning, evolving the model into an active spatial planner. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SceneReVis achieves state-of-the-art performance in high-fidelity generation and goal-oriented optimization, with improved transfer to underrepresented room categories in the dataset and promising potential for extension to out-of-distribution room types.
item.dc:creator: Yang Zhao, Shizhao Sun, Meisheng Zhang, Yingdong Shi, Xubo Yang, Jiang Bian

item.title: Thinking with Images as Continuous Actions: Numerical Visual Chain-of-Thought
item.description: arXiv:2602.23959v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent MLLMs increasingly rely on visual chain-of-thought to perform region-grounded reasoning over images. However, existing approaches ground regions via either textified coordinates (causing modality mismatch and semantic fragmentation) or fixed-granularity patches that both limit precise region selection and often require non-trivial architectural changes. In this paper, we propose Numerical Visual Chain-of-Thought (NV-CoT), a framework that enables MLLMs to reason over images using continuous numerical coordinates. NV-CoT expands the MLLM action space from discrete vocabulary tokens to a continuous Euclidean space, allowing models to directly generate bounding-box coordinates as actions with only minimal architectural modification. The framework supports both supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. In particular, we replace categorical token policies with a Gaussian (or Laplace) policy over coordinates and introduce stochasticity via reparameterized sampling, making NV-CoT fully compatible with GRPO-style policy optimization. Extensive experiments on three benchmarks against 11 representative visual reasoning baselines demonstrate that NV-CoT significantly improves localization precision and final answer accuracy, while also accelerating training convergence, validating the effectiveness of continuous-action visual reasoning in MLLMs. Project page: https://kesenzhao.github.io/NV-CoT/
item.dc:creator: Kesen Zhao, Beier Zhu, Junbao Zhou, Xingyu Zhu, Zhongqi Yue, Hanwang Zhang

item.title: Spectrum Matching: a Unified Perspective for Superior Diffusability in Latent Diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2603.14645v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the diffusability (learnability) of variational autoencoders (VAEs) in latent diffusion. We first derive distribution-free bounds on the maximum achievable reduction in pixel-space denoising loss. Under a power-law power spectral density (PSD), these bounds establish an ordering between sufficiently separated frequencies, with larger achievable reductions at lower frequencies. Motivated by this analysis and measurements of a trained pixel diffusion model, we seek to make low-frequency denoising gains useful for generating perceptually meaningful semantic content in latent diffusion. We propose the Spectrum Matching Hypothesis: latents with superior diffusability should (i) follow a flattened power-law PSD (Encoding Spectrum Matching, ESM) and (ii) preserve frequency-to-frequency semantic correspondence through the decoder (Decoding Spectrum Matching, DSM). In practice, we apply ESM by matching the PSD between images and latents, and DSM via shared spectral masking with frequency-aligned reconstruction. Importantly, Spectrum Matching clarifies prior observations of over-noisy or over-smoothed latents and provides a unified spectral interpretation of prior methods, including VA-VAE and EQ-VAE. Experiments suggest that Spectrum Matching yields superior diffusion generation on CelebA and ImageNet datasets, and outperforms prior approaches. Finally, we extend the spectral view to representation alignment (REPA): we show that the directional spectral energy of the target representation is crucial for REPA, and propose a DoG-based method to further improve the performance of REPA. Our code is available at https://github.com/forever208/SpectrumMatching.
item.dc:creator: Mang Ning, Mingxiao Li, Le Zhang, Lanmiao Liu, Matthew B. Blaschko, Albert Ali Salah, Itir Onal Ertugrul

item.title: Out-of-Distribution Object Detection in Street Scenes via Synthetic Outlier Exposure and Transfer Learning
item.description: arXiv:2603.16122v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Out-of-distribution (OOD) objects are often silently overlooked by object detectors, which produce no detection for them, leaving downstream modules with nothing to act on and no indication that anything was missed. A reliable object detector must detect OOD objects by localizing and correctly classifying them as OOD. Existing approaches primarily focus on OOD detection for image classification or rely on auxiliary branches, and typically do not treat in-distribution (ID) and OOD objects in a unified manner. We present SynOE-OD, a Synthetic Outlier-Exposure-based Object Detection method, which uses text-guided inpainting and an open-vocabulary object detector to generate and verify synthetic outliers offline. These are then used to fine-tune an object detector of choice with an added OOD class, which requires no auxiliary branch at inference time. On the OoDIS benchmark, SynOE-OD outperforms the strongest open-vocabulary baseline, reaching AP_50:95 of 57.6%, 29.4% and 39.2% on RoadObstacle, RoadAnomaly and Fishyscapes, against 48.5%, 22.7% and 22.7%. This state-of-the-art performance holds for both fine-tuned closed-set and open-vocabulary detectors while maintaining competitive ID performance in street scenes.
item.dc:creator: Sadia Ilyas, Annika M\"utze, Klaus Friedrichs, Thomas Kurbiel, Matthias Rottmann

item.title: Benchmarking Efficient & Effective Camera Pose Estimation Strategies for Novel View Synthesis
item.description: arXiv:2603.20428v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Novel view synthesis (NVS) approaches such as NeRFs or 3DGS can produce photo-realistic 3D scene representation from a set of images with known extrinsic and intrinsic parameters. The necessary camera poses and calibrations are typically obtained from the images via Structure-from-Motion (SfM). Classical SfM approaches rely on local feature matches between the images to estimate both the poses and a sparse 3D model of the scene, using bundle adjustment to refine initial pose, intrinsics, and geometry estimates. In order to increase run-time efficiency, recent SfM systems forgo optimization via bundle adjustment. Instead, they train feed-forward (transformer-based) neural networks to directly regress camera parameters and the 3D structure. While orders of magnitude more efficient, such recent works produce significantly less accurate estimates. To stimulate research on developing SfM approaches that are both efficient and effective, this paper develops a benchmark focused on SfM for novel view synthesis. Using existing datasets and two simple strategies for making the reconstruction process more efficient, we show that: (1) simply using fewer features already significantly accelerates classical SfM methods while maintaining high pose accuracy. (2) using feed-forward networks to obtain initial estimates and refining them using classical SfM techniques leads to the best efficiency-effectiveness trade-off. Our benchmark and code are publicly available at https://github.com/jhacsonmeza/sfm-benchmark-nvs.
item.dc:creator: Jhacson Meza, Martin R. Oswald, Torsten Sattler

item.title: Does Peer Observation Help? Vision-Sharing Collaboration for Vision-Language Navigation
item.description: arXiv:2603.20804v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) systems are fundamentally constrained by partial observability, as an agent can only accumulate knowledge from locations it has personally visited. As multiple robots increasingly coexist in shared environments, a natural question arises: can agents navigating the same space benefit from each other's observations? In this work, we introduce Co-VLN, a minimalist, model-agnostic framework for systematically investigating whether and how peer observations from concurrently navigating agents can benefit VLN. When independently navigating agents identify common traversed locations, they exchange structured perceptual memory, effectively expanding each agent's receptive field at no additional exploration cost. We validate our framework on the R2R benchmark under two representative paradigms (the learning-based DUET and the zero-shot MapGPT), and conduct extensive analytical experiments to systematically reveal the underlying dynamics of peer observation sharing in VLN. Results demonstrate that vision-sharing enabled model yields substantial performance improvements across both paradigms, establishing a strong foundation for future research in collaborative embodied navigation.
item.dc:creator: Qunchao Jin, Yiliao Song, Qi Wu

item.title: InverFill: One-Step Inversion for Enhanced Few-Step Diffusion Inpainting
item.description: arXiv:2603.23463v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent diffusion-based models achieve photorealism in image inpainting but require many sampling steps, limiting practical use. Few-step text-to-image models offer faster generation, but naively applying them to inpainting yields poor harmonization and artifacts between the background and inpainted region. We trace this cause to random Gaussian noise initialization, which under low function evaluations causes semantic misalignment and reduced fidelity. To overcome this, we propose InverFill, a one-step inversion method tailored for inpainting that injects semantic information from the input masked image into the initial noise, enabling high-fidelity few-step inpainting. Instead of training inpainting models, InverFill leverages few-step text-to-image models in a blended sampling pipeline with semantically aligned noise as input, significantly improving vanilla blended sampling and even matching specialized inpainting models at low NFEs. Moreover, InverFill does not require real-image supervision and only adds minimal inference overhead. Extensive experiments show that InverFill consistently boosts baseline few-step models, improving image quality and text coherence without costly retraining or heavy iterative optimization.
item.dc:creator: Duc Vu, Kien Nguyen, Ngan Nguyen, Trong-Tung Nguyen, Phong Nguyen, Khoi Nguyen, Cuong Pham, Anh Tran

item.title: The First Assessment of PhiSat-2 Imagery for Monocular Building Height Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2603.29245v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: PhiSat-2 provides multispectral observations at a 4.75m spatial resolution across geographically diverse scenes, offering a new source of remote sensing imagery for monocular building-height estimation. To comprehensively assess its utility, this study introduces the PhiSat-2--Height Dataset (PHDataset) and the Two-Stream Ordinal Network (TSONet). PHDataset integrates global PhiSat-2 imagery with open building-height references and contains 9475 co-registered patch pairs from 26 cities worldwide. In TSONet, multiscale decoupled height representation (MDHR) separates adaptive bin generation from spatial assignment, while footprint-conditioned height reconstruction (FCHR) incorporates footprint guidance at feature and reconstruction levels. Under city-disjoint evaluation, TSONet reduces building RMSE and MAE by 3.64% and 4.49%, respectively, relative to the most accurate comparison method originally designed for building-height estimation, while maintaining similar height-derived footprint IoU. Ablations support the combined design for height accuracy and footprint consistency. PhiSat-2 reduces building RMSE by 3.73% and 6.05% relative to the evaluated Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 configurations, respectively, with all seven bands providing the lowest building-height errors among its tested band subsets. LiDAR-based testing supports PHDataset-style supervision in a held-out city, while selected patch comparisons show finer urban height patterns than coarser global products. These findings highlight the value of PhiSat-2 spatial-spectral information for urban building height mapping, with PHDataset and TSONet providing a foundation for further development.
item.dc:creator: Yanjiao Song, Bowen Cai, Timo Balz, Zhenfeng Shao, Neema Simon Sumari, James Magidi, Walter Musakwa

item.title: PhyMix: Towards Physically Consistent Single-Image 3D Indoor Scene Generation with Implicit--Explicit Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2604.10125v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Existing methods for single-image 3D indoor scene generation often produce visually plausible results that violate real-world physical constraints, limiting their reliability in robotics, embodied AI, and virtual environment design. To bridge this gap, we introduce a Physics Evaluator that assesses four aspects (geometric priors, contact, stability, and deployability) through nine sub-constraints, establishing a benchmark for evaluating physical consistency. Our analysis reveals that even state-of-the-art methods produce scenes with substantial physical inconsistencies despite their visual plausibility. To address these limitations, we propose a framework that incorporates feedback from the Physics Evaluator into both training and inference to improve the physical plausibility of generated scenes. Specifically, PhyMix comprises two components: (i) implicit alignment via Scene-GRPO, a critic-free group-relative preference optimization strategy that uses physical evaluations to guide the generator toward physically plausible layouts, and (ii) explicit refinement via verifier-guided agentic repair, which translates evaluator diagnostics into executable scene-editing skills to correct residual violations at inference time. PhyMix unifies physical evaluation, preference-based alignment, and agentic inference-time correction to improve physical plausibility while retaining the observed scene content. Experiments show improvements in reconstruction quality and physical plausibility, while qualitative examples on stylized and real-world images illustrate the applicability of the framework beyond synthetic inputs.
item.dc:creator: Dongli Wu, Jingyu Hu, Ka-Hei Hui, Xiaobao Wei, Chengwen Luo, Jianqiang Li, Zhengzhe Liu

item.title: Naka-GS: Naka-Guided Chroma Correction and Point-Prior Compaction for Low-Light 3D Gaussian Splatting
item.description: arXiv:2604.11142v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Low-light inputs obscure scene content, distort color, and corrupt geometric priors, substantially degrading 3D Gaussian Splatting. Although image enhancement can recover visibility, it often introduces chromatic deviations and fine-scale artifacts that propagate through multi-view reconstruction. Moreover, dense point priors can further amplify these errors and increase optimization cost. To address the coupled challenges, we present Naka-GS, a low-light 3DGS framework that jointly improves observations and Gaussian initialization while retaining the standard 3DGS renderer and training objective. Our Naka-Guided Chroma Correction treats a fixed bionic response as a photometric anchor and learns bounded, frequency-decoupled luminance and chromatic corrections, preserving fine structures while suppressing residual color and boundary artifacts. The corrected views are reconstructed into dense scene priors, which a lightweight, non-learned Point-Prior Compaction Module refines through voxel pooling and distance-adaptive progressive pruning. On eight scene-disjoint RealX3D scenes, Naka-GS achieves 20.735~dB PSNR, 0.7408 SSIM, and 0.3340 LPIPS. PPM reduces initialization from 1.00M to 59.52K points and shortens average 3DGS optimization time by 37.7%.The code is available at https://github.com/RunyuZhu/Naka-GS
item.dc:creator: Runyu Zhu, SiXun Dong, Zhiqiang Zhang, Qingxia Ye, Rongjun Qin, Zhihua Xu

item.title: V-GIFT: Boosting Visual Instruction Tuning with Self-Supervised Guidance
item.description: arXiv:2604.12966v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) perform well on many vision-language tasks but often struggle with vision-centric problems that require fine-grained visual perception. Recent evidence suggests that this limitation arises not from weak visual representations, but from under-utilization of visual information during instruction tuning, where many tasks can be partially solved using language priors alone. We propose a simple and lightweight approach that augments visual instruction tuning with a small number of visually grounded self-supervised tasks expressed as natural language instructions. By reformulating classical self-supervised pretext tasks, such as rotation prediction, color matching, and cross-view correspondence, as image-instruction-response triplets, we introduce supervision that cannot be solved without relying on visual evidence. Our approach requires no human annotations, no architectural modifications, and no additional training stages. Across multiple models, training regimes, and benchmarks, injecting only a small fraction (3-10%) of such visually grounded instructions consistently improves performance on vision-centric evaluations.
